title: Right derived functor from a class of adapted complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for the homotopy category of integer-indexed cochain complexes and $Q_{\mathcal A}:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Equip $K(\mathcal A)$ with its triangulated structure given by shifts and cone triangles [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Let $G:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be an exact functor of triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\mathcal I$ be a class of complexes such that every complex $K$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I\in\mathcal I$, and $G(s)$ is an isomorphism whenever $s:I\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism between members of $\mathcal I$. Then there are a total right derived functor $RG:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:G\to RG\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$. They satisfy the following universal property: for every functor $T:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and natural transformation $\beta:G\to T\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$ there is a unique natural transformation $u:RG\to T$ with $\beta=(u\circ Q_{\mathcal A})\alpha$. For every $I\in\mathcal I$, $\alpha_I:G(I)\to RG(Q_{\mathcal A}I)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, right-derived assertion in Situation 05S8 (situation-derived-functor); universal property from Definition 05S9 and equation-everywhere.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=K(\mathcal A)$, $\mathcal E=D(\mathcal B)$, $Q=Q_{\mathcal A}$ and let $S$ be the quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], $S$ admits the left calculus of fractions. In particular its Ore axiom says that $s:X\to Y$ in $S$ and $f:X\to Z$ admit $a:Y\to W$ and $b:Z\to W$ with $b\in S$ and $as=bf$. Quasi-isomorphisms also satisfy two out of three: applying each cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] reduces this to cancellation and composition of isomorphisms. Choose once for each $K\in\mathcal C$ a quasi-isomorphism $r_K:K\to I_K$ with $I_K\in\mathcal I$, as the hypothesis permits. These choices need not be functorial.

source.place: Tag 04VC, definition-multiplicative-system, LMS1–LMS2; derived.tex Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, hypothesis (1).

proof.text: First define a map on each localized Hom set between adapted objects. For $I,J\in\mathcal I$ and $g:QI\to QJ$, [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-representation] gives $a_0:I\to Z$, $b_0:J\to Z$ with $b_0\in S$ and $g=Q(b_0)^{-1}Q(a_0)$. Postcompose both maps with $r_Z:Z\to I_Z$ and write $P=I_Z$, $a=r_Za_0$, $b=r_Zb_0$. Then $P\in\mathcal I$, $b\in S$, and still $g=Q(b)^{-1}Q(a)$. Define $\overline G(g)=G(b)^{-1}G(a):G(I)\to G(J)$. The inverse exists because $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism with both endpoints in $\mathcal I$, and $G$ inverts every such arrow by assumption.

source.place: Tag 04VE, lemma-morphisms-left-localization; derived.tex Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, use of replacements and hypothesis (2).

proof.text:
This value is independent of every fraction and replacement choice. If $(a_i:I\to P_i,b_i:J\to P_i)$, $i=1,2$, are two such adapted fractions for $g$, [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-equality] supplies $t_i:P_i\to W$ with $t_1a_1=t_2a_2$, $t_1b_1=t_2b_2\in S$. Each $t_i$ belongs to $S$ by two out of three, because $b_i$ and $t_ib_i$ do. Put $u_i=r_Wt_i:P_i\to I_W$. All these objects are adapted, so $G(u_i)$ is invertible, and
$$G(b_i)^{-1}G(a_i)=G(u_ib_i)^{-1}G(u_ia_i).$$
The right sides agree by the two equalities after postcomposition with $r_W$. This proves independence. For an actual arrow $f:I\to J$ between adapted objects, the fraction $(f,1_J)$ gives $\overline G(Qf)=G(f)$, including $\overline G(1_{QI})=1_{G(I)}$.

source.place: Tag 04VC, definition-multiplicative-system, following left-calculus construction: equivalence relation on arbitrary fractions (categories.tex lines 3971–3988); Tag 04VF, lemma-equality-morphisms-left-localization, treats the equal-denominator case. The cited Mathlib leaf supplies the arbitrary-denominator statement. Derived.tex Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, explicit independence behind constancy on adapted replacements.

proof.text:
The maps $\overline G$ respect composition. Let $g:QI\to QJ$ have adapted fraction $(a:I\to P,b:J\to P)$ and let $h:QJ\to QL$ have adapted fraction $(c:J\to R,d:L\to R)$. Here $b,d\in S$. Apply the left Ore axiom of [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] to $b$ and $c$ to obtain $e:P\to V$, $t:R\to V$ with $t\in S$ and $eb=tc$. Postcompose by $r_V$ and put $e'=r_Ve$, $t'=r_Vt$, $U=I_V$. Then $t'\in S$, all of $P,R,U$ are adapted, and $e'b=t'c$. In the localization, $(e'a:I\to U,t'd:L\to U)$ represents $hg$, since $Q(e')Q(b)=Q(t')Q(c)$. Thus, using Step 3 and cancelling the invertible $G(t')$ and $G(b)$,
$$\overline G(hg)=G(t'd)^{-1}G(e'a)=G(d)^{-1}G(t')^{-1}G(e')G(a)=G(d)^{-1}G(c)G(b)^{-1}G(a)=\overline G(h)\overline G(g).$$
No invertibility of $G(e')$ is used. Together with Step 3, this makes $I\mapsto G(I)$ a functor on the category with objects $I\in\mathcal I$ and morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QI,QJ)$.

source.place: Tag 04VC, definition-multiplicative-system, LMS2 and the following left-fraction composition rule; derived.tex Tag 05SA, lemma-derived-functor, expanded functoriality calculation.

proof.text:
Define $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ by $H(K)=G(I_K)$ and
$$H(f)=\overline G\bigl(Q(r_L)Q(f)Q(r_K)^{-1}\bigr)\quad(f:K\to L).$$
The identities and composition follow from Step 4 by cancelling adjacent $Q(r_L)^{-1}Q(r_L)$. If $f\in S$, the argument of $\overline G$ is an isomorphism, whose inverse is another morphism between adapted objects; Step 4 therefore makes $H(f)$ an isomorphism. Put $\alpha^0_K=G(r_K)$. To prove naturality, apply the left Ore axiom of [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] to $r_K:K\to I_K$ and $r_Lf:K\to I_L$. After replacing the common target by an adapted object $P$, obtain $a:I_K\to P$, $b:I_L\to P$ with $b\in S$ and $ar_K=br_Lf$. This is an adapted fraction for $Q(r_L)Q(f)Q(r_K)^{-1}$, hence
$$H(f)\alpha^0_K=G(b)^{-1}G(a)G(r_K)=G(r_L)G(f)=\alpha^0_LG(f).$$
Thus $\alpha^0:G\to H$ is natural. If $I\in\mathcal I$, then $r_I:I\to I_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism between adapted objects, so $\alpha^0_I$ is invertible. Moreover $H(r_K)=\overline G(Qr_{I_K})=G(r_{I_K})=\alpha^0_{I_K}$ by Step 3.

source.place: Tags 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, and 05SA, lemma-derived-functor; categories.tex Tag 04VC supplies the explicit Ore square.

proof.text: Because $H$ inverts every member of $S$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] supplies $RG:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal E$ and a natural isomorphism $\phi:RG\circ Q\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. Define $\alpha_K=\phi_K^{-1}\alpha^0_K$. This is a natural transformation $G\to RG\circ Q$. For every $I\in\mathcal I$, Step 5 makes $\alpha^0_I$ an isomorphism, so $\alpha_I$ is an isomorphism as well.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, (3), with natural isomorphism for a chosen localization; derived.tex Tag 06XN, computation on the adapted class.

proof.text:
Let $T:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal E$ and $\beta:G\to TQ$ be arbitrary. Define $v_K:G(I_K)\to T(QK)$ by $v_K=T(Qr_K)^{-1}\beta_{I_K}$. For $f:K\to L$, use the adapted Ore fraction $(a:I_K\to P,b:I_L\to P)$ from Step 5. Naturality of $\beta$ at $a,b$, with $G(b)$ and $T(Qb)$ invertible, gives
$$v_LH(f)=T(Qr_L)^{-1}\beta_{I_L}G(b)^{-1}G(a)=T(Qr_L)^{-1}T(Qb)^{-1}\beta_PG(a)=T(Qr_L)^{-1}T(Qb)^{-1}T(Qa)\beta_{I_K}=T(Qf)v_K,$$
where the last equality is $ar_K=br_Lf$ after applying $TQ$ and cancelling. Hence $v:H\to TQ$ is natural. Also $v_K\alpha^0_K=T(Qr_K)^{-1}\beta_{I_K}G(r_K)=\beta_K$ by naturality at $r_K$. Both $H$ and $TQ$ invert $S$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], using $\phi:RGQ\cong H$ and the identity $TQ\cong TQ$, now supplies $u:RG\to T$ with $u_{QK}=v_K\phi_K$. Therefore $u_{QK}\alpha_K=v_K\alpha^0_K=\beta_K$ for all $K$, as required.

source.place: Tag 05SA, lemma-derived-functor, comparison compatibility expanded; equation-everywhere following definition-everywhere-defined; categories.tex Tag 04VG and the fully faithful natural-transformation localization property in the cited node.

proof.text:
For uniqueness, let $u':RG\to T$ satisfy $u'_{QK}\alpha_K=\beta_K$, and put $w_K=u'_{QK}\phi_K^{-1}$. Then $w:H\to TQ$ is natural and $w_K\alpha^0_K=\beta_K$. Naturality at $r_K$, and the final equality of Step 5, yield
$$T(Qr_K)w_K=w_{I_K}H(r_K)=w_{I_K}\alpha^0_{I_K}=\beta_{I_K}.$$
Since $T(Qr_K)$ is invertible this forces $w_K=T(Qr_K)^{-1}\beta_{I_K}=v_K$. Consequently $u'_{QK}=v_K\phi_K=u_{QK}$ for every $K$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives $u'=u$. This proves exactly the stated right-derived universal property and completes the computation assertion from Step 6.
